The swimming pool at Naval Colony, Kanjurmarg, operated under the Michael Phelps Swimming brand, charges a very high rate for the general public (non-Naval), which comes to around ₹600–₹800 per visit when calculated from their package rates.

While the premium pricing is justified in their advertisements by the claim of temperature-controlled water, the reality is different — the temperature control system has not been operational for the past two years. Based on discussions with regular users, the reason appears to be an unresolved dispute between the Navy and the Michael Phelps Swimming management regarding electricity bill payments. Unfortunately, there is no sign of this being resolved soon.

New customers are still enrolled with temperature control advertised as a key USP, without disclosure of the ongoing issue. This amounts to misleading information.

For Naval employees, the rates are minimal, making it a great facility. However, for the general public, given the lack of temperature control, the pricing feels unreasonable.

Pros:
Good training facility and structured programs
Ideal for Naval employees due to subsidized rates

Cons:
Very high rates for non-Naval public
False/misleading advertisement regarding temperature control
No clarity on resolution of the temperature control issue

Recommendation:
If temperature control matters to you, speak to current regular users before enrolling.

featured_reviews.name: Marie Rose
featured_reviews.review_text:
This review is only for those parent(s) who are from middle class background and who know basic swimming that was learnt from their parents or from a professional and who are expecting that their child would pick basic swimming in their 60 sessions of Michael Phelps at Sahar Plaza Andheri East.

I would not recommend this place and instead if you have a pool within your society take your kid there and teach swimming as it is not rocket science but only practice. I enrolled my six year old daughter on 05/11/2025 with expiry on July 5, 2026 for 60 sessions as you can see from the swimming card. I was told that first 12 sessions was making the kid comfortable in water, gliding in water and jumping into water without fear which my daughter did. In reality, she was doing this for 15 sessions till I took them to task and asked them when they would start teaching her swimming that only then did they began her swimming classes. My kid was happy in the pool and was picking swimming quite well with confidence till 18th March on the 28th session when the head coach asked me about renewal as there was an offer going on. I told the coach that my expiry was not due and I will do it at that time irrespective of the offer. After that on the 29th session, the instructor who was teaching my kid started behaving oddly with my kid. He would instead of focussing on her swimming, started holding her when she was swimming or when she was jumping in water. Suddenly, in that one day, my daughter told me that if she didn’t swim properly, she would drown. The next session, I again noticed the same behaviour in the instructor and I realized that the instructor was hitting the confidence of my daughter by holding her hand when she jumped in the water which was never done with her. That was the last session of my daughter with Michael Phelps and on that day I gave earful to the head coach and questioned how the instructor had undermined the confidence of my kid. I told the head coach that till date the instructor never held the hand of my daughter whenever she jumped into the water and why did he hold only her hand and not the hand of any other kids who had jumped in the water. On hindsight, I realized that since I did not commit a renewal when asked to do so, the coaches decided to slow the progress of learning swimming of my kid so that I would do another 60 sessions and what is worse is for greed of money they hit the confidence of my kid in water by instilling fear of drowning so much so that it took me another 8 sessions in the pool of my society to rectify this fear. I decided to forgo the remaining 30 sessions of my daughter as I don’t want to entrust her with teachers who instilled fear instead of positive learning and it takes a long time to unlearn that instilled fear.
Coming to my background, I learnt swimming from my mother in a local pond in 10 days and so did my husband. After that, I sharpened my swimming with breathing technique in 15 days by a trainer. All my instructors be it my mother or the trainer told me only one thing – Be free in water and water will always push you upwards and the moment you struggle you will sink, so just be free in water and feel the water. This was a positive learning that I got about swimming. This learning takes time but it is positive learning and helps in swimming. The moment you talk to a child about drowning, the child learns fear not swimming.

So for those parents who think that their kid will learn swimming here in 60 sessions, its not going to happen without a renewal at Michael Phelps. The techniques taught here are all good but when a kid’s confidence is hit, it is difficult. If you have the money, then honey Michael Phelps is for you.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am sharing this review to give honest feedback about this swimming centre.

The teachers and reception staff are generally helpful and sincere. One teacher noticed that my child was losing confidence and adjusted the training, which we really appreciated.

However, there are some areas where improvement is needed, especially since many young children attend these classes.

1. Cold Weather Conditions
Since this is an outdoor pool, strong winds blow directly onto the students during monsoon and winter. It feels cold even for parents sitting outside, and it is difficult for children after they come out of the water. When we raised this concern, we did not receive clear solutions.

2. Temperature-Regulated Pool
The pool is said to be temperature regulated, which is one reason we enrolled. However, during winter we were told that the heater was not working and would be started later. The water remained quite cold, making it difficult for children to complete their sessions comfortably.

3. Communication
Most staff members are polite, but one or two people sometimes speak in a way that feels a bit rude. A more friendly tone would help parents feel more comfortable.

4. Pool Support
There are no support rods or bars along the pool walls for children to hold. These would be helpful for beginners.

5. Washroom Facilities
Many mothers come with young children, but there is only one shower in the female washroom. Because of this, some people have to leave without washing after swimming.

Overall, the teachers are good, but some improvements in facilities and planning would make the experience much better for children and parents.

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent visit to Nahar's Nectarfield clubhouse left me with mixed feelings. On one hand, the clubhouse boasts an impressive array of facilities, including a stunning swimming pool, baby pool, basketball and tennis courts, badminton facilities, a well-equipped gym, a salon, and spacious banquet halls, all thoughtfully designed and meticulously maintained. The physical infrastructure is undoubtedly commendable.

However, the shining exterior contrasts starkly with the glaring shortcomings of the staff. It's regrettable to report that the staff's performance was far from satisfactory. Their conduct lacked basic courtesy, and interactions with them were often uncomfortable. Furthermore, their knowledge of the clubhouse's rules and regulations left much to be desired, resulting in frequent confusion and frustration among visitors and members alike. It seemed that the staff had no clue about the rules, and every member seemed to receive different information, creating a perplexing and chaotic atmosphere.

What was perhaps most disappointing was the staff's apparent lack of empathy. They seemed disinterested in addressing concerns or providing assistance, failing to create the warm and welcoming atmosphere one would expect at a club of this caliber.

It was also disheartening to note that regardless of whether one was a guest, a member, or a child, the staff's level of service remained consistently lacking. This lack of differentiation in service levels was a glaring issue.

Furthermore, the pricing structure at Nahar's Nectarfield raised eyebrows. The fees, even for residents of Nahar's Amrit Shakti, appeared unjustifiably high. Guest charges, in particular, bordered on the exorbitant, making it less accessible for those wishing to enjoy the facilities on occasion.

Lastly, the on-site restaurant, while aesthetically pleasing, left much to be desired in terms of service and food quality. Surprisingly, it did not cater to non-vegetarian preferences, even though members are non-vegetarian enthusiasts.

In conclusion, Nahar's Nectarfield clubhouse presents an impressive array of amenities and infrastructure. However, the staff's professionalism, or rather the lack thereof, and their inability to provide clear, consistent information regarding rules and policies, cast a shadow over the overall experience. Urgent improvements in staff training, people skills, and customer service are essential to bring this otherwise promising establishment up to par with its potential. Additionally, a reevaluation of pricing and an enhancement of the restaurant's offerings would further contribute to making Nahar's Nectarfield a truly exceptional destination for its members and guests.

featured_reviews.name: Hemanth Poojary
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of Mumbai’s most well-planned and versatile sports complexes. It truly stands out as a one-stop gymkhana offering an impressive range of facilities under one roof.
The complex offers multiple sports options including Swimming, Rifle Shooting, Gymnastics, Table Tennis, Pickleball, Roller Skating and more, making it suitable for children, professionals, fitness enthusiasts and competitive athletes alike.
The infrastructure is modern, clean and well maintained, creating a great environment for training and recreation.
A big highlight is the Sollasa Sports Café, which serves quality food at reasonable prices—perfect for a healthy meal or quick snack after a workout or a game.
The Sports Recovery Centre is another major attraction, featuring Sauna, Steam, Massage and Hydrotherapy facilities, giving athletes and fitness lovers a professional space to recover and rejuvenate.
The Terrace Turf is ideal for a quick game of football and cricket, offering a great playing experience with a city view.
Complex also has at least two well-sized halls that are perfect for engagements, birthday parties, naming ceremonies, society meetings, and small get-togethers.
All in all, Prabodhan Thackeray Krida Sankul is a true one-stop destination for sports, fitness, recreation and social gatherings, offering excellent value for money and a wide variety of facilities rarely found together in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prabodhankar Thackeray Swimming Pool is the only swimming facility of its scale in and around Vile Parle, making it a highly sought-after destination for fitness enthusiasts and learners of all ages. Getting admission to the swimming classes can be a challenge due to the high demand, but those who manage to secure a spot find the experience worthwhile. The pool caters to various age groups and skill levels, offering batches throughout the day.

Beyond swimming, the complex has developed into a multi-sport hub. It features facilities like pickleball courts, carrom tables, a small cricket turf, and even a well-equipped gymnastics hall, attracting young athletes and hobby players alike. There is also a small sports shop inside the premises where basic sports equipment and accessories are available.

One of the highlights many visitors appreciate is the canteen. Known for its omelette and poha, it serves fresh, satisfying snacks and also offers a decent missal that regulars enjoy after their sessions.

The place is fairly well maintained and serves as a much-needed sports center for the residents of Vile Parle. With its growing range of facilities and community-friendly atmosphere, it continues to be an important recreational and fitness landmark in the locality.
